title: Cutting his own lip and the overwork of the Terrace
summary: Asked for his biggest kicks, Thomas names Henderson's band, tells how he cut his own lip with a razor blade in Chicago in 1936, and says the work was too rough to allow expression.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Where would you say you had yourx biggest kicks playing? Off the top of your head.
I never had any kicks playing. Never. What do you mean by kicks?
Well, I mean where do you think you had the most pleasure playing? I mean with Smack's band or where?

Oh, Smack's band, of course. Yeah, sure. I tell you what it was it was a matter of musicianship. It was a matter of wanting to be there and what Baby is talking about Louis Armstrong and Pops, I had a little thing here. I took a knife and razor blade and cut this ... out of my chops. Yeah, you know, kids do a lot of things. But I wanted to beat that.
Oh, you mean when you with Smack.
Yeah, the work was too rough. Nobody supposed to work that rough. Nobody way in hell should work as hard as we worked. Not to get ... full expression to the people.
Earl Hines has told me the same thing about ... very high.
It's ridiculous. It's ridiculous because in the first place if you do those kind of things, as we did, you don't have full expression yourself. If music is anything, it's expression.
